newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda says rebels seize 21 people from seminary.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says rebels seize 21 people from seminary.

text.p: Ugandan rebels of the Allied Democratic Forces have abducted 19 Roman Catholic seminary students and two staff from southwest Uganda, military sources said on Monday.
They said a total of 39 students and two workers from Saint John's Seminary in Kasese district were abducted on Saturday but 20 of the students had managed to escape by Sunday morning.

"These rebels took the children as porters, as shields, and have taken them into the mountains. The military is in pursuit but we have to be careful not to anger the kidnappers," Minister of State for Defence Minister Amama Mbabazi told Reuters.
He said the rebels shot and wounded two students during the attack, some 380 km (235 miles) west of the Ugandan capital.
State radio described the abductors as "bandits".
In a separate development, military sources said six rebels of the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) were killed by troops on Thursday and Friday near the northern Ugandan town of Gulu.
Uganda says ADF rebels operating in the mountains of the west and at times in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire, are supported by Sudan, a charge denied by Khartoum.
Uganda has accused Sudan's government of arming the LRA and giving it bases in government-held parts of southern Sudan. Khartoum accuses Uganda of backing Sudanese rebels in southern Sudan.
